newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end slightly lower on Sakakibara comments.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end slightly lower on Sakakibara comments.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures ended slightly lower on Thursday as sentiment was weakened by overnight comments by a senior Finance Ministry official, traders said.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, said on Wednesday that although monetary policy was in the hands of the Bank of Japan, there was political pressure to raise the official discount rate.
Traders said the comments led to worries about a possible rise in interest rates and invited selling of JGBs.

"Some politicians have called for a rise in the official discount rate. It is true that there is an atmosphere among politicians to raise the official discount rate," Sakakibara told currency dealers at a foreign exchange conference.

The impact on JGBs was limited, however, as market players were sceptical about whether the comments would actually lead to an earlier-than-expected change in the Bank of Japan's monetary policy, traders said.
Some market participants now feel that the BOJ may raise interest rates in July, but such players still comprise a minority, a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
"Traders overall have been buying JGBs recently based on the view that the BOJ will not raise interest rates in the first half of the current business year," the trader said.

"The majority in the market still feels that interest rates will not be raised until autumn and I don't think the situation has changed. Sakakibara may be an authority on monetary policy, but he is not the final arbiter of interest rates," he said.
The June ended at 126.62, down from the previous day's close of 126.76. Turnover was 44,766 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.185 percent as of 0639 GMT, up from the previous day's close of 2.150 percent.
Traders said investor buying of medium- and long-term cash JGBs on dips limited the downside of JGBs.
Investors such as investment management firms were detected buying cash JGBs, the trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
But long-term cash JGBs were generally heavy, as other investors were detected shifting their investment toward JGB futures and medium-term JGBs, a brokerage house trader said.
City banks and life insurers who had been buying long-term cash JGBs since the beginning of this month, have started to sell, the trader said.
Talk of activity by hedge funds is also dampening market sentiment, traders said.
There is a rumour that a U.S. hedge fund has been buying out-of-the-money JGB futures put options in large lots, they said.
Foreign financial institutions have also been selling JGB futures, and seem to be taking a more bearish view of the market than their Japanese counterparts, a trust bank trader said.
